---

You can make the markers selectable by tap instead of long-pressing the tiny context-menu hitboxes.

What you have now (long-press on a transparent rectangle):  
```491:516:miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceMapView.swift
Rectangle()
    .foregroundColor(.clear)
    .contentShape(Rectangle())
    .frame(width: 80, height: 120)
    .offset(y: 12)
    .zIndex(1)
    .contextMenu { ... }
```

Practical tap-first options:
- Add a tap gesture to the same transparent rectangle that opens an action sheet/confirmationDialog or a bottom sheet with the same actions (edit/navigation/history), and keep the contextMenu as a fallback for iPad/Mac. Example to adapt in the rectangle above:
  ```swift
  .onTapGesture {
      selectedDeviceID = device.DeviceID
      showDeviceActionsSheet = true   // drive a confirmationDialog/sheet
  }
  ```
- If multiple devices overlap, on tap show a small picker list for that coordinate (e.g., a bottom sheet listing the nearby device names), then let the user pick which device’s actions to run.
- Slightly enlarge the hit area further (e.g., 120x160) and center it over the marker; make sure `.contentShape(Rectangle())` remains so taps land reliably.

Suggested UI pattern:
- iPhone: tap → confirmationDialog/Menu; long-press still opens context menu.
- iPad/Mac: keep contextMenu, but also allow tap to show a popover/bottom sheet; if multiple devices are within a small distance threshold, present a list to choose the target.

This keeps it “tappable” while preserving your existing actions and avoids the precision problem when markers overlap.
